facts.t: Judicial guidelines are meant to be temporary and rarely are
facts.d: Directions issued until legislation is enacted routinely outlive that phrase. Vishaka governed workplace harassment for sixteen years; the police reforms in Prakash Singh have never been fully legislated at all.

facts.t: The Court has reversed its own legislation
facts.d: Rajesh Sharma (2017) created family welfare committees to screen section 498A complaints. The Supreme Court modified its own scheme shortly afterwards — an unusual admission that judicially crafted procedure can misfire.

facts.t: A PIL produced the Central Vigilance Commission Act
facts.d: Vineet Narain's binding directions on CBI autonomy and vigilance structure were eventually codified by Parliament in the CVC Act of 2003. Judicial legislation converted into actual legislation — the exception rather than the rule.

bank.q: Match List I (case) with List II (judicial creation):
pairs: 2. Regulation of acid sales and rehabilitation
3. State Police Commissions and fixed tenures
4. Disclosure of candidates' criminal and financial background
bank.e: Police reform, adoption rules, acid-sale regulation and candidate disclosure respectively.

bank.q: With reference to Vishaka, consider the following statements:
s: The guidelines filled a legislative vacuum on workplace sexual harassment.
They remained operative until the POSH Act of 2013.
Parliament enacted the statute within two years of the judgment.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Sixteen years passed between the guidelines and the statute.

bank.q: Which one of the following is NOT a criticism of judicial legislation?
o: It lacks democratic legitimacy, bypassing debate and scrutiny
Courts lack institutional capacity for long-term implementation
It provides a constitutional safety valve when Parliament delays
Temporary judicial law tends to become de facto permanent
bank.e: That is listed among the justifications, not the criticisms.

bank.as: Repeated judicial legislation can weaken executive responsibility.
bank.rs: When courts routinely supply the remedy, public pressure shifts away from the legislature and executive.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — described as government by judiciary, with the dilution of democratic pressure as its cost.

bank.q: Which judgment created committees to check misuse of section 498A, later modified by the Court itself?
o: Rajesh Sharma v. State of UP
bank.e: Rajesh Sharma (2017), whose family welfare committee scheme the Supreme Court subsequently modified.

s: Sunset clauses making judicial guidelines valid only until legislation is enacted.
Codified criteria for when judicial directions may substitute legislation.
Public consultation through amicus curiae and expert panels before framing policy-like directions.
bank.e: All three, alongside prompt legislative responsiveness to judicial observations.

bank.q: All of the following resulted in eventual legislation EXCEPT:
bank.e: The Prakash Singh directions have never been comprehensively legislated — states have implemented them only partially.

bank.q: Which principle is invoked to discipline judicial legislation?
o: The doctrine of pith and substance
bank.e: Restraint anchored in necessity — the courts should legislate only where the constitutional gap genuinely demands it.

bank.q: Consider the following statements about the tension judicial legislation creates:
s: Speed is achieved at the cost of deliberation, research and inclusivity.
Constitutional morality can come into conflict with political morality.
Judicial creativity is inherently incapable of responding to technological change.
bank.e: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Swift response to technology, environment and gender justice is cited among the advantages of judicial creativity.

bank.as: Kesavananda Bharati is itself an instance of judicial legislation.
bank.rs: It propounded a wholly new constitutional principle limiting Parliament's amending power, with no textual basis.
bank.e: Both true and the Reason explains the Assertion — the basic structure doctrine is the largest single act of judicial creation in Indian law.
